--- page 1 ---
Cover + table of contents: UN Anticipatory Action Framework, Nigeria - Floods, as of July 2026, endorsed by the ERC on 27 July 2026. Sections 1-10 (triggers p8, activities p14, financing p19, annexes p23).
--- page 2 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Executive summary: US$6M pre-arranged ($5M CERF + $1M NHF), up to 764,864 people, 7 Adamawa LGAs on the Benue River (Fufore, Yola South, Yola North, Girei, Demsa, Numan, Lamurde). Two triggers: (1) riverine action+readiness (CERF and NHF); (2) flash-flood observational trigger (NHF only) for 4 BAY-state LGAs (Mobbar, Maiduguri, Geidam, Jere). Readiness trigger: GloFAS ensemble mean discharge > 3,132 m3/s at Wuroboki (G5004) within first 12 days of leadtime, or GloFAS reanalysis > same; RP ~1-in-3 yrs; fired up to 10 days ahead of action trigger; not met before action trigger in 2012 and 2018. CERF funds cover one activation within 2 years of ERC endorsement; NHF approved for 2026; WFP co-financing $2M.
--- page 3 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Action trigger: >=6 of 10 selected Google GRRR gauges (of 42 GloFAS+Google gauges) on the Benue simultaneously exceed their individual 4-yr RP thresholds (~1,100-1,117 m3/s per gauge) on the same day; overall RP ~1-in-4.5 yrs; fires up to 5 days before a 1-in-4 yr flood. Flash-flood monitoring thresholds (flood exposure, people): Mobbar 14,720; Maiduguri 23,740; Geidam 5,501; Jere 103,612; equal trigger probability per LGA, overall RP ~4 yrs. Action plan: MPCA, in-kind, early warning, services; CERF to UN agencies, NHF to national NGOs.
--- page 4 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Lessons/changes (phased triggers, adjusted CERF envelope, actionable early warning, improved targeting, NHF complementary). Validity: CERF pre-arranged funding valid 2 years (2026 and 2027 seasons); NHF used by end of 2026.
--- page 5 ---
Figure: "Nigeria seasonal and risk convergence calendar - TIMELINE: 2025 Floods" (Jan-Dec, weeks 1-52). Rainy season ~May-Nov; floods ~Jul-Oct; land prep Mar-May, planting May-Jul, weeding Jul-Oct, harvest Oct-Dec. Early warning: global & national (GloFas, Google Hub, NiMet, NIHSA) and community-based systems marked from ~Jun onward. Action windows: Readiness ~Mar-Jun (10-15 days lead time); Anticipatory Action (AA) ~Jun-Sep (5-7 days lead time); (Early) Response ~Jul-Oct. Inset map: Adamawa State vulnerability hotspot, with the southern LGAs (Lamurde, Numan, Demsa, Girei, Yola, Fufore) highlighted in blue. Text: 2024 floods hit 34 of 36 states (Borno worst), 2025 floods affected >400,000 people in 25 states, 232 deaths; Govt of Nigeria preparing up to $60M for AA (14 states along Benue and Niger rivers, plus 4-5 flash flood pilot states); WFP matched US$2M.
--- page 6 ---
Figure: Nigeria 2025 HNRP flow diagram: Strategic planning "Future risk 2025" (Climate/seasonal: Floods, Disease outbreak-Cholera; Non-climate: Conflict) maps to Operational planning: Preparedness Plan ($25m), Anticipatory Action Plan ($10m), Rapid Response Mechanism ($10m). Text: Nigeria draft NAP framework; 5% of 2026 HNRP programmed resources for cyclical events such as floods.
--- page 7 ---
Figure: HNRP strategic objective chart (Nigeria 2025 HNRP): three priorities with budgets - Build readiness and preparedness (Nov-June, $25 million, 9 activities); Anticipatory action (post trigger, 7-10 days lead time before shock, $10 million, 7 activities: RCCE, multipurpose cash, shelter kits, latrine desludging, drainage, immunization, Aqua tabs); RRM respond (post trigger 1-72 hours after shock, $10 million, 17 activities). Text: lessons from 2025 activation in Adamawa (assistance sometimes arrived too close to/after flood onset); 2024 NHF allocation $2M for Bama (Borno) and Numan (Adamawa), ~276,600 people exposed.
--- page 8 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Trigger working group (NiHSA, NiMet, NEMA, NASRDA, OCHA CHD); NiHSA and NEMA historical data validated triggers. Repeats the two-trigger mechanism, readiness trigger (3,132 m3/s at Wuroboki, G5004) and action trigger definitions; if readiness is reached, only readiness activities and the readiness fraction of funds are authorized.

Floodscan >=4-yr RP events: 1999, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2022, 2023.
Table: Trigger Mechanism Statistics. Stats by trigger (analysis years 1998-2023 action, 2003-2022 readiness): Readiness RP 3.5 yrs, activation prob 29%, years 2003, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2019, 2022; Action RP 4.5 yrs, prob 22%, years 1998, 1999, 2012, 2018, 2019, 2022. Overall stats (2003-2022): overall RP 3.0 yrs; overall probability of activation 33%; average total spending per year $1.0M; average period for total budget spend/effective RP 4.1 yrs; probability of total budget spend 24%; average total spending per year with activation $2.9M. Flash flood thresholds repeated (Floodscan SFED flood extent x population).
--- page 10 ---
Table: Activation protocol - riverine flooding (When/Who/What/How). Monitoring June to end Dec by OCHA CHD (GloFAS and Google FloodHub, daily automated emails). Readiness trigger reached: CHD informs RC/HC, CERF, NHF, Core AA WG, NEMA, NiHSA, NiMet (email + WhatsApp); CERF immediately sends pre-approved approval letters; partners implement readiness activities only; optional meeting (not on whether to activate). Action trigger reached: CHD informs; CERF sends approval letters (or confirms authorization of readiness+action portion if readiness preceded); NHF fund manager authorizes action portion; partners begin implementing.

Plus last table row: partners begin implementing after CERF/NHF approval.

Map: Northeast Nigeria showing CERF riverine (7 LGAs, blue, southern Adamawa along Benue) vs NHF flash flood (4 LGAs, red: Mobbar, Maiduguri, Geidam, Jere in the north - Borno/Yobe). Flash-flood LGAs chosen from NiHSA 2026 projections and 2026 HNRP prioritisation. Household targeting text: National Social Registry (NSR) via NASSCO covers ~19 million vulnerable individuals, plus community validation; WFP, IOM, LESGO use common registry.

Narrative text, no figure. Partner lessons (WFP two-tier activation, FAO, WHO, UNICEF); NRCS leads joint early warning. Financing: ERC pre-agreed up to $5M from CERF only if riverine triggers reached; disbursed on no-regrets basis when readiness or action trigger reached. Scenarios A (all-systems go: readiness then action), B (false alarm: readiness only), listed.
--- page 20 ---
Tables: Scenario B-2 (false alarm then readiness+action within max 6 months), C (action trigger without readiness), D (no activation). NHF $1M envelope by sector: Joint targeting and Early Warning $300,000; Protection (child protection & GBV) $200,000; Multisectoral (MPCA) $500,000. NHF scenarios: 1 riverine trigger reached - $1,000,000 to 7 LGAs; 2 riverine not reached by end of peak season (~mid-September) but flash flood trigger met - TBD early response in flash-flood LGAs; 3 neither - TBD reprioritised. Start of funding table.

--- page 24 ---
Figure: "Adamawa - Historical trigger timing (1998-2023)" dot/timeline chart, x axis date Aug 01-Nov 01, y axis year 1998-2023; markers: action trigger (red tick), readiness trigger (blue tick), max flood extent (grey dot), 3/4/5-yr RP flood extent (orange/purple bubbles). Criteria: GloFAS RA or RF <=12d >3,132 m3/s (2003+ only); GRRR >=60% of gauges >= 4-yr RP. Examples: 2012 action 18 Aug, readiness 21 Aug, floods 23-27 Aug; 2022 readiness 19 Aug, action 29 Aug, 5-yr flood 09 Sep; 2018 action 08 Sep, flood 12 Sep; 2019 readiness 31 Aug, action 11 Oct, flood 30 Oct; 1998 action 21 Sep; 1999 action ~02 Sep, floods 02 and 18-21 Oct; 2003 readiness 28 Aug; 2015 readiness 04 Sep, flood 31 Aug-04 Sep; 2016 readiness 04 Sep; 2014 readiness 28 Aug; 2023 flood 06-07 Oct. Footnote: GRRR trigger date estimated from reanalysis shifted 5 days earlier. Text: nine OCHA core principles begin (multi-sectoral, protection centrality, gender equality, accountability/PSEA, localization).
